Requirements are written on core-passport keys (temperature.range, temperature.base, pressure.base, vacuum.available, optical_access, sample.diameter.max, cryogen.type, magnetic_field.max) wherever the physics allows, plus the family keys the procedure genuinely needs (process.freeze_drying, temperature.condenser.min, process.dsc, process.cryogenic_milling, milling.*, rf.frequency.range, purge.gas, chamber.volume, optical.transmission_range, temperature.stability, gas.flow_rate.max). experiments.name: Matrix-isolation FTIR spectroscopy of a sublimed heterocycle in solid argon at 15 K with broadband UV photolysis
experiments.plain_name: Trap single molecules in frozen argon and study them with infrared light
experiments.description: A heterocyclic compound is sublimed and co-deposited with a large excess of argon onto a CsI window held at 15 K inside a closed-cycle helium cryostat evacuated to about 3.5e-5 mbar; mid-IR spectra (4000-400 cm-1) are recorded on the isolated monomers and followed through broadband UV irradiation from a 500 W Hg(Xe) lamp. This is the standard matrix-isolation route to conformers, photoproducts and reactive intermediates in chemistry.

requirements.rationale: The matrix is deposited and held with the optical substrate at 15 K; the machine must be able to reach and hold that sample temperature.

requirements.quote: onto a CsI optical substrate, cooled down to 15 K.

requirements.rationale: Argon matrix isolation needs a base temperature of 15 K or lower; a machine whose lowest temperature is above 15 K cannot form a rigid Ar matrix.

requirements.quote: onto a CsI optical substrate, cooled down to 15 K.

requirements.rationale: Deposition and spectroscopy happen inside an evacuated chamber; an atmospheric-pressure cold space would frost the window and destroy the matrix.

experiments.name: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of a pharmaceutical multicomponent crystal at 100 K in an open-flow nitrogen cryostream
experiments.plain_name: Work out a medicine's crystal structure while a cold gas jet keeps it at 100 K
experiments.description: Co-crystals and salts of two anti-tubercular drugs with pyridoxine are mounted on a diffractometer and held at 100 K by an open-flow liquid-nitrogen cryostream (Oxford Cryosystems Cryostream 800) while Mo-K-alpha data are collected. Cooling to 100 K suppresses thermal motion and solvent loss and is routine for structure determination of active pharmaceutical ingredients.

requirements.rationale: The whole data collection is made with the crystal held at 100 K.

experiments.name: Pharmaceutical lyophilization cycle in vials: freezing at -50 C, primary drying at -10 C and 180 mTorr, secondary drying at 40 C
experiments.plain_name: Freeze-dry a medicine into a shelf-stable powder
experiments.description: A nucleic-acid lipid-nanoparticle drug product is frozen on the shelves at -50 C, primary-dried at a shelf temperature of -10 C under 180 mTorr chamber pressure and secondary-dried at 40 C (optimised variant: -15 C primary, 30 C secondary) in a pilot freeze dryer, with the sublimed water captured on the ice condenser. This is the standard cycle structure for parenteral lyophilised drug products.

requirements.rationale: The shelves must span the whole recipe, from the -50 C freezing step to the 40 C secondary-drying step.

experiments.name: Modulated DSC of a frozen biopharmaceutical formulation: equilibration at -70 C and 1 C/min ramp to determine the glass transition of the freeze-concentrate
experiments.plain_name: Find the temperature at which a frozen medicine mixture softens
experiments.description: A liquid vaccine formulation is sealed in a hermetic Tzero pan, equilibrated at -70 C, held for 5 minutes and ramped at 1 C/min to 100 C with heat-cool temperature modulation, so that the glass transition of the maximally freeze-concentrated solution can be read from the reversing heat-flow signal. That transition sets the maximum allowable product temperature of the subsequent freeze-drying cycle.

requirements.rationale: The measurement cycle runs from an equilibration at -70 C up to 100 C in one ramp, so the sample space must cover that whole span.

experiments.name: Cryogenic impact milling of a crystalline drug under liquid nitrogen for 2.5 h at 9 impacts per second to produce the amorphous form
experiments.plain_name: Grind a medicine into powder while liquid nitrogen keeps it brittle
experiments.description: Crystalline bosentan is milled in a stainless-steel grinding vessel immersed in liquid nitrogen in a Retsch CryoMill at an impact frequency of 9 cycles per second for a total of 2.5 h, converting it to the amorphous state without the thermal degradation that ambient milling or melt-quenching would cause. The amorphous product is then compared with the melt-quenched glass.

requirements.rationale: The grinding jar is held at liquid-nitrogen temperature (-196 C = 77150 mK) throughout, which is what embrittles the drug and stops it recrystallising or degrading during milling.

requirements.rationale: The procedure consumes liquid nitrogen: the milling vessel is physically immersed in it, so a purely mechanical or electrically cooled machine cannot reproduce the process.

experiments.name: Cryogenic messenger-tagging infrared ion spectroscopy in a 30-45 K trap at 2e-6 mbar
experiments.plain_name: Identify a molecule by chilling its ions and shining infrared on them
experiments.description: Mass- and mobility-selected ions are stored in a cryogenic ion trap held between 30 and 45 K by a closed-cycle helium cryostat, where a pulsed 20% N2/80% He gas mixture forms weakly bound messenger-tagged complexes at about 2e-6 mbar; a tunable mid-IR source is stepped in 2 cm-1 steps from 990 to 1810 cm-1 and tag loss gives a diagnostic vibrational fingerprint. This is how isomeric small molecules, glycans and drug metabolites are distinguished when mass spectrometry alone cannot.

requirements.rationale: The trap is operated between 30 and 45 K, tuned for the analyte; outside that window the messenger tag either does not bind or does not detach cleanly.

requirements.quote: maintained between 30 and 45 K (adjusted for optimal tagging of different analytes)

requirements.rationale: Tagging requires the trap to be able to reach 30 K; a machine with a higher base temperature cannot condense the N2 messenger onto the ions.

experiments.name: Frozen-sample EPR of a transition-metal catalyst: X-band CW at 77 K in a liquid-nitrogen finger dewar and Q-band pulsed HYSCORE at 40 K and 1224.1 mT
experiments.plain_name: Detect unpaired electrons in a deep-frozen catalyst sample
experiments.description: Chromium-doped silicoaluminophosphate molecular sieves are characterised by continuous-wave X-band EPR (about 9.5 GHz) with the sample cell in a liquid-nitrogen finger dewar at 77 K, and by Q-band (about 33.8 GHz) pulsed HYSCORE at 1224.1 mT and 40 K, to locate the chromium site and its coordination. Freezing the sample is what narrows the lines and makes the hyperfine couplings resolvable.

requirements.rationale: The study needs both the 77 K continuous-wave measurement and the 40 K pulsed measurement, so the sample space must cover 40-77 K.

experiments.name: Variable-temperature X-ray powder diffraction of a drug solvate from 293 K to 103 K in 10 K steps in a capillary
experiments.plain_name: Cool a drug powder step by step and watch its X-ray pattern change
experiments.description: Nifedipine solvates are loaded into 0.7 mm borosilicate capillaries and measured on a Cu-K-alpha-1 powder diffractometer while an open-flow nitrogen cryostream steps the temperature from 293 K down to 103 K, capturing patterns every 10 K with a 5 minute hold at each step, which reveals a phase transition at 143 K. Variable-temperature powder diffraction is the standard way to map solid-form stability of an active pharmaceutical ingredient.

requirements.rationale: The series runs continuously from room temperature (293 K) down to 103 K, so the machine must cover that whole span on one sample.
